title: Does a gate or a RANSAC start survive the mismatch mixes a real SIFT matcher produces?
lede: with the mismatch rates and along/near/far mixes measured for SIFT, a ratio test of 0.8 or tighter (10% wrong or fewer) leaves gate and RANSAC-start adjustment near the clean floor (0.002 to 0.02 radii) while an all-view start is 0.005 to 0.39; at ratio 0.9 the RANSAC start wins and with no ratio test (56% wrong) everything fails. Synthetic rig, measured mixes
summary: Takes the next step of sensing-matchreal: its measured ratio-test mismatch mixes (rate and the share along the epipolar line, near and far) are injected into the sensing-epigate rig of 12 views with wrong poses. At ratio 0.7 (6% wrong, 62% along) Cauchy-loss adjustment from an all-view start gives 0.052 object radii, a RANSAC start 0.0060, an epipolar gate 0.0038 and gate plus RANSAC start 0.0036, against a clean floor of 0.0014. At ratio 0.9 (23% wrong) the RANSAC start (0.088) beats the gate (0.17); with no ratio test (56% wrong on stereo, 40% on warped photographs) every method is above 0.4. The gate beats the RANSAC start up to 20% contamination at the ratio-0.7 shares and fails at 30%. The mismatch statistics are measured; the scene, poses and Gaussian noise are the synthetic rig's, mismatches are independent per observation, and there are 6 seeds with no intervals.
